Operator ask (2026-08-29): clean up old Claude remote sessions, investigate why some agents look
old-and-still-connected, and end up with hourly cleanup running natively inside Antiphon - not via
an external Windmill/SSH schedule.

## What I checked live before filing this (both currently healthy, evidence attached)

**claude.ai remote sessions (CARD-0144's domain):** ran `scripts/cleanup-claude-sessions.ps1
-RequireDisconnected:$false` (report-only). Result: `candidates=0 skipped=39 liveBridges=16`. The
oldest disconnected session is 3.1 days old, well under any staleness threshold - nothing to clean
right now. CARD-0144's weekly Windmill job (server2, SSH into this Windows box) is doing its job.

**Zombie OS processes (CARD-0221/CARD-0229's domain):** ran `scripts/reap-zombie-agents.ps1`
fresh. Result: 0 positives, 0 unidentified, every one of 17 live agent-shaped processes classified
`Z4 not a zombie class (warm/standing/live)` or `Z6 too young to judge yet`. Tonight's CARD-0221
(pool-release fix) and CARD-0229 (janitor false-failure fix) already closed the two live bugs that
were producing real zombies before tonight.

**A red herring I chased and want on record so it isn't re-investigated:** `task-da2c3589`
(a Shared pool delegate) briefly looked like a stuck-Running zombie - its task settled Succeeded,
got pooled warm (`Idle`+`PoolIdleSince`+`PoolReservedForRootTaskId`) at 17:38:58, then showed
`Status=Running` with those fields cleared again minutes later. Traced via the server log: this
is the pool-reuse feature working exactly as designed - a follow-up Shared task (my own CARD-0165
retry, `43e4a6f9`) picked up the warm delegate at 17:53:34 and put it back to work. Not a bug.

## So what's actually true right now

Nothing is currently broken. What genuinely exists: two SEPARATE cleanup mechanisms
(claude.ai remote-session archival, zombie-process reaping) each implemented as a standalone
PowerShell script, each intended to run on a schedule EXTERNAL to Antiphon (Windmill on server2,
SSHing back into this Windows machine to run a script) rather than as a job the Antiphon server
itself owns and runs. CARD-0232 (Windmill schedule for the zombie script) is closed in favor of
this card's direction.

## What to investigate and build

1. **Read both existing scripts in full** (`scripts/cleanup-claude-sessions.ps1`,
   `scripts/reap-zombie-agents.ps1`) and assess whether their logic can be ported into a native
   .NET `BackgroundService` inside the Antiphon server, modeled on the existing
   `WorktreeJanitorHostedService` pattern (`server/Infrastructure/Git/WorktreeJanitorHostedService.cs`)
   and the pool janitor (`AgentTaskDispatcher.RetireIdleWarmAgentsAsync`) - both already run on a
   timer inside the server process with no external scheduler.
2. **claude.ai cleanup** needs an outbound HTTPS client using the Claude Code CLI's own OAuth
   token from `~/.claude/.credentials.json` (same auth CARD-0144's script already uses) - confirm
   this is safely readable/usable from a long-running server process (token refresh lifecycle,
   whether the file can be watched vs re-read per run, whether running from the server changes any
   safety assumption CARD-0144's design relied on, e.g. its "human gate before first live run"
   precedent - a NEW automated surface should get the same one-time supervised-run treatment
   before going unattended).
3. **Zombie-process reaping** needs `Process`/WMI enumeration from within the .NET server, which
   is a materially different environment than a PowerShell script shelling out - check whether the
   existing script's identity ladder (I1-I5) and classification rules (Z1-Z7) port cleanly to
   `System.Diagnostics.Process` or need rework, and whether running this INSIDE the server process
   (which is itself one of the things being surveyed) introduces any new self-referential risk.
4. **Cadence: hourly**, per the operator's ask - both mechanisms currently run weekly (claude.ai)
   or on-demand only (zombie reap, never scheduled at all). Confirm hourly is safe for both (no
   API rate-limit concern for claude.ai's admin endpoints at that frequency; no meaningful
   CPU/IO cost concern for a process census).
5. **Decide: one unified hosted service, or two separate ones?** They have different
   trigger domains (external API vs local OS) and different blast radii (claude.ai calls touch the
   operator's real account; process reaping touches this machine only) - a single card should not
   presuppose the answer, but should recommend one after reading both scripts.
6. **Migration path for the two existing scripts**: keep them as operator-invokable manual tools
   (dry-run census/report is still useful for out-of-band checks) even after a native scheduled
   job exists, or retire them once the native path is proven - recommend, don't presuppose.
7. **Safety**: the claude.ai half touches the operator's real account. Any native automated version
   should default to report-only until manually promoted to executing, mirroring CARD-0144's own
   S4 human-gate precedent - do not skip that step just because it's now "in Antiphon" rather than
   a standalone script.

## Explicitly not asking for in this card

- Immediate implementation - this is an investigate-then-plan card, matching this session's usual
  pipeline (Plan -> review -> Build -> verify).
- Any change to CARD-0144's or CARD-0221's already-shipped, already-working detection LOGIC - this
  is about WHERE and HOW OFTEN that logic runs, not what it decides.
EOF
